problem:
The acceleration $a$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
a(t)=⟨6t-2,4⟩.
$$

Given that the particle is at the position $(0,0)$ and has velocity $⟨1,\,4⟩$ when $t=1,$ calculate the position vector of $P$ at time $t.$

activity_context.topic_title: Finding Displacement Vectors in Two Dimensions Using Integration

feedback.problem:
The acceleration $a$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
a(t)=⟨-{e}^{-t},\,20{t}^{3}⟩.
$$

Given that the particle is at the position $(3,-2)$ and has velocity $⟨0,\,1⟩$ when $t=0,$ calculate the position vector of $P$ at time $t.$

$r(t)=⟨${{field-1}}$,\,{t}^{5}+t-2\,⟩$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the position vector, we need to integrate the velocity vector. To find the velocity vector, we first need to integrate the acceleration vector. 

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨-{e}^{-t},\,20{t}^{3}⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int (-{e}^{-t})\,\text{d}t,\,\int 20{t}^{3}\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{-t}+{C}_{1},\,5{t}^{4}+{C}_{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $v(0)=⟨0,1⟩.$ Substituting $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(0) & =⟨{e}^{0}+{C}_{1},\,5(0)^{4}+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨0,1⟩ & =⟨1+{C}_{1},\,{C}_{2}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so, we must have ${C}_{1}=-1$ and ${C}_{2}=1.$ Therefore, the velocity vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =⟨{e}^{-t}-1,\,5{t}^{4}+1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the position vector by integrating the velocity vector.

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨{e}^{-t}-1,\,5{t}^{4}+1⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int ({e}^{-t}-1)\,\text{d}t,\,\int (5{t}^{4}+1)\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨-{e}^{-t}-t+{C}_{3},\,{t}^{5}+t+{C}_{4}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $r(0)=⟨3,-2⟩.$ Substituting $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0) & =⟨-{e}^{0}-0+{C}_{3},\,{0}^{5}+0+{C}_{4}⟩ \\ ⟨3,-2⟩ & =⟨-1+{C}_{3},\,{C}_{4}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so, we must have ${C}_{3}=4$ and ${C}_{4}=-2.$ Therefore, the position of $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
r(t)=⟨-{e}^{-t}-t+4,\,{t}^{5}+t-2⟩.
$$
